hero.title: Ace Your Hiring Manager Round
hero.subtitle: The person who will be your boss is evaluating you
hero.description: The Hiring Manager round is uniquely personal. Unlike other interviewers who evaluate specific competencies, the HM is asking: 'Do I want this person on MY team? Will they make ME more successful?' Understanding this dynamic is the key to winning this round.

whatIsHMRound.title: What is the Hiring Manager Round?
whatIsHMRound.subtitle: The most personal and often decisive interview
whatIsHMRound.overview: The Hiring Manager (HM) round is typically 45-60 minutes with your potential direct manager. For senior roles, the HM has significant influence over the final hiring decision. They're evaluating not just your skills, but whether you'll complement their team, bring new capabilities, and make their life easier. This is about fit, chemistry, and vision alignment.

keyFacts.label: Duration
keyFacts.description: Usually one session, sometimes in the loop

keyFacts.label: Interviewer
keyFacts.description: The person you'll report to if hired

keyFacts.label: Focus
keyFacts.description: Leadership style, team dynamics, strategic alignment

keyFacts.label: Weight
keyFacts.description: HM's opinion often carries the most weight in decisions

whatHMEvaluates.description: Do you bring skills or perspectives the team currently lacks? Will you elevate the team?
whatHMEvaluates.example: If the team is strong technically but weak on stakeholder management, showing this strength is gold.

whatHMEvaluates.description: Will your management approach work with theirs? Can you operate independently within their framework?
whatHMEvaluates.example: If the HM is hands-off, they want someone who doesn't need micromanagement.

whatHMEvaluates.description: Do you share their vision for the team and organization? Can you help execute their strategy?
whatHMEvaluates.example: Understanding their priorities and showing how you'd contribute to them is powerful.

whatHMEvaluates.description: Will you create problems or solve them? Are you someone who makes the HM's job easier?
whatHMEvaluates.example: Senior hires who bring drama or need hand-holding are immediately filtered out.

whatHMEvaluates.description: Do they enjoy talking to you? Would they want you in their weekly 1:1s?
whatHMEvaluates.example: Being likable, thoughtful, and articulate matters more here than in other rounds.

roleSpecificPrep.title: HM Round by Role
roleSpecificPrep.subtitle: What each HM is looking for in senior candidates

roles.title: Engineering Manager / Sr. Engineering Manager
hmWants: Someone who can own a team end-to-end without escalating everything
A leader who develops talent and doesn't hoard top performers
Strong execution - hitting deadlines without sacrificing quality
Someone who handles people issues before they become the HM's problem
Technical credibility to earn respect from the team
keyQuestions: How would you handle inheriting a team with performance issues?
Tell me about your approach to developing senior engineers
How do you balance autonomy for your team with alignment to org goals?
What's your approach when you disagree with your manager's direction?
roles.showThem: You can run a team independently, handle the messy people stuff, and deliver consistently.

roles.title: SRE Manager / Sr. SRE Manager
hmWants: Someone who prevents fires, not just fights them
A leader who can influence product teams to prioritize reliability
Balance between SRE idealism and business pragmatism
On-call culture expertise - preventing burnout while maintaining coverage
Data-driven approach to reliability investments
keyQuestions: How do you convince product teams to invest in reliability?
What's your philosophy on error budgets and when to enforce them?
How do you structure on-call rotations for a 24/7 service?
Tell me about a time you had to push back on a launch for reliability reasons
roles.showThem: You bring proactive reliability leadership, not just reactive firefighting.

roles.title: Production Manager / Technical Program Manager
hmWants: Someone who makes cross-team coordination effortless
A communicator who can represent the program to executives
Proactive risk identification - no surprises
Influence without creating friction with engineering teams
Someone who gets things done without constant oversight
keyQuestions: How do you build relationships with engineering leads who see TPMs as overhead?
Tell me about a time you had to escalate to save a program
How do you handle competing priorities across teams you don't control?
What's your approach to program status communication?
roles.showThem: You drive results through influence and make complex coordination look easy.

roles.title: Director of Engineering
hmWants: A partner who can own a major part of the organization
Strategic thinking combined with execution excellence
Someone who develops managers, not just engineers
Executive presence for stakeholder and board interactions
Ability to navigate organizational politics gracefully
keyQuestions: How do you balance innovation with operational excellence?
Tell me about building a management team from scratch
How do you handle organizational change and resistance?
What's your approach to technical debt at an org level?
roles.showThem: You're a true partner who can own major org initiatives and develop the next generation of leaders.

roles.title: VP of Engineering
hmWants: A thought partner on engineering strategy and culture
Someone who can represent engineering to the board and investors
Executive who can navigate M&A and major transformations
Builder of world-class engineering organizations
Someone with industry credibility and network
keyQuestions: How do you think about engineering as a competitive advantage?
Tell me about a major organizational transformation you led
How do you build engineering culture at scale?
What's your approach to CEO/board communication?
roles.showThem: You're a transformational leader who elevates engineering as a strategic function.

roles.title: Principal/Staff Architect
hmWants: Technical vision that aligns with business strategy
Ability to influence without formal authority
Someone who uplevels the entire engineering organization
Practical architecture, not ivory tower thinking
Strong communication for non-technical stakeholders
keyQuestions: How do you drive adoption of architectural standards?
Tell me about a time you had to kill a project or technology
How do you balance innovation with stability?
What's your approach to mentoring senior engineers?
roles.showThem: You bring practical technical leadership that moves the entire org forward.

winningStrategies.title: How to Win the HM Round
winningStrategies.subtitle: Strategies that consistently work

strategies.description: Look them up on LinkedIn. Understand their background, how long they've been at the company, and their career trajectory. Reference this naturally in conversation.
strategies.example: I noticed you built out the SRE function here from scratch - I'd love to hear about that journey.

strategies.description: HMs are hiring because they have problems to solve. Show you understand what those problems might be and how you'd help.
strategies.example: It sounds like the team is growing fast. I've scaled teams through that exact phase and know the challenges.

strategies.description: HMs love talking about where they want to take their org. Get them talking about their vision and show how you'd contribute.
strategies.example: Where do you see the team in 18 months? What capabilities do you want to build?

strategies.description: Show you're someone who solves problems, not creates them. Reference times you handled issues independently.
strategies.example: I believe in solving problems at my level before escalating. Here's an example of how I handled...

strategies.description: The best HM interviews feel like mutual exploration, not interrogation. Show genuine interest in the role and team.
strategies.example: Ask follow-up questions. Engage with their answers. Make it a conversation.

strategies.description: End by expressing clear interest and asking about next steps. Don't be passive.
strategies.example: I'm very excited about this role. It aligns perfectly with where I want to grow. What are the next steps?

commonMistakes.title: HM Round Mistakes
commonMistakes.subtitle: Why senior candidates fail this round

mistakes.mistake: Treating it like a skills test
mistakes.reality: The HM already knows you have the skills (you passed the phone screen). This is about fit and chemistry.
mistakes.fix: Focus on demonstrating how you'd work within THEIR specific context.

mistakes.reality: HMs want to see that you're genuinely interested in solving their problems, not just getting a job.
mistakes.fix: Ask questions like: What's keeping you up at night? What would success look like in 6 months?

mistakes.reality: The HM round is more personal. Being stiff signals you might be hard to work with.
mistakes.fix: Be professional but personable. Show your authentic self.

mistakes.reality: Not knowing anything about your potential boss signals lack of preparation and interest.
mistakes.fix: Spend 15 minutes on LinkedIn. Find common ground or talking points.

mistakes.reality: HMs have good BS detectors. They also don't want someone who seems unsure of themselves.
mistakes.fix: Be confident but honest. Acknowledge what you're still learning.

mistakes.reality: Ending passively makes you seem uninterested or unsure.
mistakes.fix: Express genuine interest and ask about next steps.

questions.question: What would success look like for this role in the first 90 days?
questions.why: Shows you're thinking about impact and sets clear expectations

questions.question: What's the biggest challenge facing the team right now?
questions.why: Shows you want to understand problems you'll need to solve

questions.question: How would you describe your management style?
questions.why: Shows you care about the working relationship

questions.question: What does the path to promotion look like from this role?
questions.why: Shows you're thinking long-term and growth-oriented

questions.question: What made you join this company, and what keeps you here?
questions.why: Builds personal connection and gives insight into culture

questions.question: What capabilities do you wish the team had that they don't today?
questions.why: Identifies gaps you might fill - very strategic
